answer:
Your reading is right. The implementation behaved correctly and the script's pass condition was wrong. I reproduced the failure exactly offline.

**Why both occurrences sit inside the recall block.** The setup check found no marker in `state.before[recallIndex]`. That snapshot is the full list pi sends: system messages, assistant history and the stubbed tool results. So if the model had echoed the marker anywhere (Derek's candidate 2), the run would have exited 2. That rules candidate 2 out. `recallProblems` then showed that every message stayed the same except the latest user message, which gained one block carrying the marker. The prompt-3 text carries no marker, and a recalled item's label never carries one. So the payload's two occurrences mean two recalled items. Each `emit_marker` call archives its own ~950-character copy, past `minCharsToArchive` 600. Jev answered yes to both, and both were recalled into one block, as the spec requires.

**Offline reproduction** (a `git archive 0911062` mktemp copy, Derek's stand-in, dummy key, no model call):

| Stand-in variant | Exit | Printed line |
|---|---|---|
| One tool call, unchanged | 0 | PASS |
| Two parallel calls (`tool_calls` index 0 and 1) | 1 | "prompt 3's payload carries the marker 2 times, not once" |
| Two sequential calls | 1 | the same line |

In both failing variants the instrumented run showed `markerCalls=2`, two recalled items, the marker twice in the block, twice in the post list and twice in the payload, and nowhere else. The live run cannot say whether the model called twice or an OpenRouter stream quirk made pi run the tool twice; the remedy does not need to know.

**The ruling: (c), which is (b) made measurable.** The payload must carry the marker exactly as many times as the appended recall block does, and at least once, which `recallProblems` already requires. Because the setup check proves the history is marker-free, this one equality also catches pi dropping the block, duplicating it, or putting the marker anywhere else.

I reject (a). Requiring one call would make every double call exit 2, spending money for a run that proves nothing. A double call is also the better live case, because it exercises multi-item recall.

**The script change, run in my copy.** Add a helper `lastBlockText(snapshot)` returning the text of the last block of the snapshot's latest user message. Replace the `!== 1` check with:

`const inBlock = recallProblemsFound.length > 0 ? 0 : occurrences(lastBlockText(state.after[recallIndex]), marker); if (occurrences(recallPayload, marker) !== inBlock) problems.push(`prompt 3's payload carries the marker ${…} times, but its recall block carries it ${inBlock} times (emit_marker ran ${state.markerCalls} times)`);`

It takes a two-line comment saying why: the model may call the tool more than once, and the history is marker-free by setup check. Results, offline through the stand-in, with no model call:

| Run | Exit | Note |
|---|---|---|
| One call | 0 | PASS |
| Two parallel calls | 0 | PASS |
| Two sequential calls | 0 | PASS |
| `--break-model` | 1 | only the "no recall block … gained 0 block(s)" line, which is exactly 9.2's named condition; before, it also printed "0 times, not once" |
| Key unset | 2 | |
| Mutation: marker added to the payload outside the block | 1 | "3 times, but its recall block carries it 2 times" |
| Mutation: marker stripped from the payload | 1 | "0 times, … 2 times" |

The mutations used a test-only `before_provider_request` hook in my copy; it is not part of the remedy.

**Routing.** The condition is stated in two places: `design.md` decision 13 (5) at L382 and `tasks.md` 9.2 at L138. Bambadjan amends both to the same sentence: "the marker appears in that request's provider payload exactly as many times as the recall block carries it, and at least once — once per archived `emit_marker` output, since the model may call the tool more than once; setup check (6) keeps the history marker-free". Nothing else in decision 13 changes. Derek then makes the script change above and re-runs it offline through the stand-in, once with one call and once with two, plus `--break-model`. I review that small script diff before any paid run.

**Another paid run is needed.** 9.2 ticks only on a recorded exit 0 and a recorded `--break-model` exit 1 under the amended script. The run at 0911062 cannot tick it. That means one passing run and one `--break-model` run, both already authorized by Joel's Q5 ruling. The failed run's line can be recorded as context, but it is not one of 9.2's two completion lines.
decided_by:
**The condition being narrowed is mine.** Stage 2 resolution COMP-4 wrote decision 13 (5)'s "the marker appears exactly once in that request's provider payload". It rested on an unstated assumption of exactly one `emit_marker` call, and my gate-2 offline checks ran only the single-call stand-in. This correction narrows that condition. It does not reopen Joel's Q5(a), which makes the script the thing that ticks the box and authorizes its runs.

Measured offline: two tool calls reproduce the live line exactly, and the remedy passes for one and two calls and catches both payload mutations.
